content.text:
I read every input file, the full draft, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and traced each limitation, numeral, structure, relationship, material, and figure statement to an affirmative inventor passage.

Key traces performed:

- **Claims 1–20**: rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter terminating in a bearing face, non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air, extraction rate maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, pressure-differential holding without operator force, all-rigid vibration path free of elastomer/foam/resilient mount, sliding while held, PTFE/plastic/metal/combination materials, vacuum pump, handle for guiding, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control, and stirring elements producing constant forward motion — each maps to disclosure.md or to the one technical USER message ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion").
- **Numerals 10–48**: all seventeen are defined once, used consistently, and every one appears in at least one figure brief and in the description; no stray or duplicate meaning; the 26→34 gap is unused, not dangling.
- **Figure briefs vs. Brief Description**: FIG. 2's sectioned bodies (base, chamber, perimeter member, covering element) versus the elevation housing match the brief; FIG. 5 and FIG. 6 omissions match; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same designation in the source view (FIG. 3), the resulting views (FIGS. 2 and 4), and draft/07.
- **Depiction conventions**: the rectangular ring, slab/block outlines, gap through the base, flat bearing-face end, and stirring-element number/position are each disclaimed inside the briefs only. The application text stays shape-, port-, and location-neutral; no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaks into the specification, so nothing broadens an embodiment to justify a renderer's choice.
- **No notes, placeholders, questions, or instructions** remain in any section; operational USER messages ("resume", "regenerate", "five sheets") were treated as context, not disclosure.

No unsupported technical assertion or internal inconsistency was verified, so I return an empty findings array.

input.summary: Full ledger built and cleared. Every limitation of claims 1-20 (rigid base with first and second sides; vibration motor coupled to the first side; air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber; rigid low-friction perimeter member extending from the second side at its perimeter, surrounding the chamber and terminating in a bearing face that is its end face; a clearance along at least part of the member through which ambient air enters; a volumetric extraction rate sufficient to keep the chamber below atmospheric pressure while air keeps entering; the resulting pressure differential holding the device without operator downward force; an all-rigid vibration transmission path with no elastomeric member, foam member or resilient mount; slidability of the bearing face while the differential is maintained; closed-loop restriction without a complete airtight seal; plastic, metal, PTFE or combinations; freedom from rubber, elastomer and foam with rigid contact; continuous extraction; vacuum pump; guiding handle; rope, wire or cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control; and one or more stirring elements producing constant forward motion) was traced to an exact affirmative inventor passage in disclosure.md, except the stirring-element and autonomous-movement matter, which traces to the single technical USER message "the device is already connected via vaccum and unlike other machines it is free to move, so we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand, we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". All seventeen numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes one thing, each is defined in the numeral table, each appears in the detailed description, and each is carried by at least one figure brief with no stray numeral and no numeral used for two parts; the unused 28-32 gap leaves nothing dangling. All six figure briefs and the six paragraphs of the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared item by item: the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned bodies (base, chamber, perimeter member, covering element) against the hatched slab, legs and band with the air-extraction housing in unhatched elevation; the FIG. 3 ring and inner face against "showing the second side and the perimeter member"; the FIG. 4 column, bearing face, clearance, covering element, bonding material and substrate against the enlarged fragmentary recital; the FIG. 5 and FIG. 6 omission recitals against the briefs' omitted bodies. Both named section lines carry the same repeated designation in the source view, the resulting view and the drawing description: 2-2 appears in the FIG. 3 brief, the FIG. 2 view line and draft/07 FIG. 2; 4-4 appears in the FIG. 3 brief, the FIG. 4 view line and draft/07 FIG. 4. Depiction conventions were tested against the functional-surface rule: the rectangular ring plan, schematic slab and block outlines, the unhatched gap reading as fluid communication, the flat lower end of the perimeter member, and the number, form and position of the stirring elements are each declared schematic and confined to the figure briefs, and none verbalizes taper, angle, runout, depth ordering, radial or circumferential end position, or contact topology beyond the disclosed "rigid contact with the tile" and air "entering beneath the rigid perimeter". Contact at section 2-2 and clearance at section 4-4 correspond to the disclosed simultaneous condition and to the claimed "along at least part of the perimeter member", with the angular positions expressly disclaimed. The application text was checked for leakage of renderer choices and contains no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other embodiment added to justify a visual choice; it remains shape-, port-, mounting- and location-neutral. Claims and description use identical relationships and terms (perimeter member, bearing face, clearance, exposed face, covering element, vibration transmission path), the prior-art "sliding base" is kept lexically distinct from the claimed base 12, and the Background's two-problem framing has its antecedent restored. Prior-art characterizations with [REF:] markers were treated as exempt from inventor support and left to the later citation trace. Operational USER messages to resume, rebuild, regenerate, preserve or tighten, and their figure and sheet counts, were treated as context only and not as technical disclosure. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section; title, cross-reference, government-support statement, applicant and inventor match brief.md; the abstract is a single paragraph of 145 words with no means-plus-function language. No untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
